industry.crude: Brent averaged US$70.45/bbl in FY26 (US$78.91 in FY25) and traded US$60-70 for most of the year; the West Asia (Strait of Hormuz) crisis from March 2026 sent it to ~US$97-98 in Q1FY27 (ONGC call) and ~US$96 in Jul-Sep 2026. EIA (9-Sep-2026) expects ~US$90 in 2H2026, US$77 in Q2-2027 and ~US$67 in 2H2027 as shut-in output returns (2027 average US$74).
industry.india: India produced 27.95 MMT of crude (-2.6%) and 34.78 BCM of gas (-3.7%) in FY26; import dependence 88.7% (Mar-2026). ONGC: 73% of crude, 57% of gas (AR FY26).
industry.policy: Gas from old (nomination) fields is priced by formula with a cap (US$7.00/mmBtu in FY27 vs a US$9.00 formula price in Sep-2026), so ONGC does not keep the upside on ~76% of its gas; new-well gas (24% of Q1FY27 sales) gets 1.2x the formula price uncapped. Crude is sold at Brent-linked prices. Windfall tax (SAED) Jul-2022 to Dec-2024 took ₹23,800 cr from ONGC; not re-imposed by 30-Sep-2026. Royalty cut 8-May-2026 (offshore crude 9.09%->8%, gas 10%->8%). Samudra Manthan: ₹84,084 cr government deepwater exploration scheme.

excluded.HINDPETRO: Distorted: HPCL lost ₹12,265 cr in Q1FY27 (marketing under-recoveries after the Hormuz crisis), so its trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 (~45x) is ~9x its five-year median; it also had loss quarters inside the window. It is also ONGC's 54.9% subsidiary.

street.method: Mostly a sum of the parts: standalone earnings on a P/E of 6.3-8x (FY28E, Dec-27E or Jun-28E), plus the listed stakes at market less a 20-25% holding discount (Geojit 50%), and ONGC Videsh valued separately (JM 7x FY28E EPS = ₹7/share; MOSL 0.5x FY25 book = ₹23/share). BOB Caps applies 6.5x to consolidated EPS and adds only IOC, GAIL and Petronet. JM uses FY28E standalone EPS before dividend income ('core', ₹29.2).

stockEvents: Covid and oil crash: share fell to ~₹66 (13-Mar-2020)
Windfall tax (SAED) on domestic crude imposed
Sakhalin-1 stake restored to OVL (accounted from Jan-2026)
West Asia / Strait of Hormuz crisis: Brent spikes; ONGC rallies to ~₹300 (Apr-May 2026)
Royalty rates cut on offshore crude and gas
Share falls to ~₹233 as HPCL's under-recovery losses and windfall-tax fears weigh
Q1FY27: record standalone PBT ₹22,848 cr; HPCL loss ₹12,265 cr
moat: Scale and incumbency in Indian upstream (73% of crude, 57% of gas; nomination acreage held since before 1999; 518 MMtoe of 1P reserves); but a price-taker on crude, a price-controlled seller on 76% of its gas, with mature fields declining 5-8% a year. No pricing power; the advantage is access to acreage and infrastructure, and the cost of capital of a sovereign-backed company.
critiques: Production has not grown in five years: standalone crude 19.3-19.6 MMT since FY22, gas down from 20.9 to 19.5 BCM; KG-98/2 oil has disappointed.
Policy takes the upside: windfall tax (₹23,800 cr in FY23-25), the APM cap, and pressure to share OMC losses (HPCL, its own subsidiary, lost ₹12,265 cr in Q1FY27).
Capital allocation is directed by the state: HPCL (₹36,915 cr in 2018), OPaL (₹21,181 cr invested, still loss-making in Q1FY27), and deepwater exploration under Samudra Manthan.
Consolidated earnings are hostage to OMC marketing margins; standalone is what most of the street values.
Contingent liabilities: Panna-Mukta-Tapti arbitration ₹15,216 cr where ONGC chose not to defend itself at the ministry's request.
gaps: FY27 royalty rate by field: we apply the announced cuts to the FY26 mix; ONGC's own estimate of the saving is not in our sources.
